assumption: Sekakah = Qumran or its wadi; conditional
rank_meaning: Investigative priority within the Qumran hypothesis, not numerical probability

geometry.method: Manually sampled positions and simplified linework from inspected source images; each plan retains its own frame.
geometry.uncertainty: Pixel sampling is approximate; original survey positional accuracy and geographic tie are unknown. Highlight radii have no spatial-confidence meaning.

ilan1989.excludes: Length break near point 18; tunnel inset; regional inset

candidates.name: Visible channel start · Ilan point 3
candidates.support: Best functional match for the head of the whole aqueduct. Located at a small ravine on the northern bank.
candidates.limit: No particular great stone identified. A northern bank does not resolve the wording’s grammatical ambiguity.
candidates.test: Find a view showing the boulder, pothole and wall together and trace their channel to the small ravine. A two-tunnel plan alignment supports the same upstream sector but cannot fix the intake at the rock.

candidates.name: Large rock beside upstream collection works
candidates.support: Reeder describes an approximately 3 m-high boulder incorporated into the works beside the upstream channel.
candidates.limit: The landmark noun is restored. Its required northern relationship, ancient phase and correspondence with point 3 remain unproved.
candidates.test: Match the boulder–pothole–wall sequence to the small-ravine outlet beside Ilan point 3; retain the main-wadi proposed dam as a separate feature.

candidates.name: Branch junction and short western tunnel
candidates.support: Possible beginning of a collecting branch or subsection. Short tunnel probably corresponds to Reeder Tunnel 2.
candidates.limit: Needs a subsection-head reading. Branch function and flow direction differ among published interpretations.
candidates.test: Compare channel-floor elevations and branch connections.

candidates.name: Long eastern tunnel · western mouth
candidates.support: Reeder Fig. 2 and Magen Fig. 87 visually match the same long-tunnel mouth. Magen’s text supports its western/upstream attribution; Ilan point 11 and Reeder Tunnel 1 remain probable plan correspondences.
candidates.limit: Downstream of the intake. Reeder calls the photo an exit and Magen an entrance; the visual match itself establishes neither hydraulic direction nor a scroll identity.
candidates.test: Find a photographic sequence from this western mouth through both internal openings. The inspected interior image does not locate each fissure individually.
